llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly downloads the saved .docx from the VM after postconfig saves it (Ctrl+S), ensuring the evaluated state reflects agent changes.
Getter accesses doc.paragraphs[0] which is the standard python-docx representation of the first paragraph, matching the instruction target.
Getter checks all(run.italic is True for run in para.runs) which correctly uses strict identity check; when a user applies italic via Ctrl+I, python-docx sets run.italic=True explicitly.
Metric correctly compares actual italic state against expected_italic=True and returns 1.0/0.0.
Negative control resistance is present: initial state of the document has no italic formatting, so it will correctly fail the check.
Empty-runs edge case returns italic=False which correctly fails the expected=True check.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: doc.paragraphs[0] could be a heading or empty paragraph if the .docx file has structural elements before the first body paragraph. Consider adding a check or comment to verify paragraph[0] is indeed the intended first body paragraph for this document.

Minor: run.italic is True does not catch italic formatting inherited from a paragraph or character style (italic=None in python-docx). If the document uses style-based italic, the evaluator would incorrectly return False. Consider adding a fallback check using the paragraph/style effective italic value if needed.
